bg-31-01.hint: I give a birthday present to a friend.
bg-31-01.why: Target person receives -한테 (spoken) or -에게: 친구한테 생일 선물을 줘요.

bg-31-01.q: State that you gave a gift to your younger sibling. Use 동생 + recipient particle -한테, 선물 + object particle -을/를, and 주다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-31-01.why: 동생 is the recipient marked with -한테.

steps.en: I give a gift to my friend.
I give a birthday gift to my close friend.

ko: 그래서 어제 백화점에서 산 선물을 친구한테 주었어요.
en: Today is my close friend's birthday.
So I gave the present I bought yesterday at the department store to my friend.
My friend was very happy receiving the present.

bg-31-01.why: The text says '제 친한 친구의 생일이에요'.

bg-31-01.q: How did the friend feel when receiving the gift?
options: The friend was surprised and angry
bg-31-01.why: The passage states '친구가 선물을 받고 아주 기뻐했어요'.

items: I can use -에게 and -한테 to indicate the recipient of an action.
I can politely address elders with -께 when giving or speaking.

bg-31-02.hint: Yesterday I received a letter from a friend.
bg-31-02.why: Source person uses -한테서: 친구한테서 편지를 받았어요.

bg-31-02.q: State that you received a phone call from a friend. Use 친구 + source particle -한테서, 전화 + object particle -을/를, and 받다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-31-02.why: 친구 is the source of the phone call marked with -한테서.

steps.en: I received a letter from a friend.
Yesterday I received a long letter from a hometown friend.

ko: 오후에 우체통을 확인했는데 편지 한 통이 들어 있었어요.
오래전에 외국으로 이사 간 친구한테서 온 편지였어요.
친구에게서 오랜만에 소식을 듣게 되어 정말 반가웠어요.
en: In the afternoon I checked the mailbox and found one letter inside.
It was a letter from a friend who moved abroad long ago.
I was really glad to hear news from my friend after a long time.

bg-31-02.q: Where did the letter come from?
options: From a friend who moved abroad
bg-31-02.why: The text says '외국으로 이사 간 친구한테서 온 편지였어요'.

bg-31-02.q: How did the writer feel after receiving the letter?
options: Really glad to hear from the friend

items: I can express receiving or learning something from someone using -에게서 and -한테서.
I can distinguish the recipient (-한테) from the source (-한테서).

bg-31-03.hint: I commute to the company by subway.
bg-31-03.why: Means ending in ㄹ batchim takes -로 (not -으로): 지하철로!

bg-31-03.q: Give directions telling someone to go to the right at the traffic light. Use 오른쪽 + direction particle -(으)로 and 가다 + -(으)세요.
bg-31-03.why: 오른쪽 ends in a consonant (ㄱ), taking -으로 for direction.

steps.en: At that intersection, please go to the right.
At that big building intersection, please go straight to the right.

ko: 회사까지 버스나 지하철로 갈 수 있어요.
하지만 아침에는 길이 막히기 때문에 지하철로 가는 것이 더 빨라요.
지하철역에서 내려서 오른쪽으로 조금만 걸어가면 회사가 나와요.
en: You can go to work by bus or by subway.
However, because the roads are jammed in the morning, going by subway is faster.
If you get off at the subway station and walk just a little to the right, the office appears.

bg-31-03.q: Why is the subway preferred in the morning?
options: Because the subway is completely free
Because there are no buses running
bg-31-03.why: The text explains '아침에는 길이 막히기 때문에'.

bg-31-03.q: Which direction should you walk after getting off at the station?

items: I can express directions (left, right, straight) using -(으)로.
I can express means of transport, tools, and language using -(으)로, remembering the ㄹ batchim rule.

bg-31-04.hint: I sent a greeting letter to my teacher.
bg-31-04.why: Honorific particle -께 is used for respected teachers: 선생님께.

bg-31-04.q: State that you go to the station by subway. Use 지하철 + transport particle -(으)로 and 가다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-31-04.why: 지하철 ends in ㄹ batchim, requiring -로 for means of transportation.

bg-31-04.q: Fix the particle error in using a tool/instrument.
bg-31-04.hint: 연필 ends with the ㄹ batchim, so it takes -로 without 으: 연필로.
bg-31-04.why: Nouns ending in ㄹ batchim take -로, not -으로: 연필로.

a.d: Used when directing an action, speech, or object toward a human or animal receiver.
ex: 친구**한테** 선물을 줘요. / I give a gift to my friend.

b.d: Used when indicating a spatial direction toward a location, or a tool/transport method used.
ex: 지하철**로** 학교에 가요. / I go to school by subway.

bg-31-04.tip: Use -에게/-한테 for living recipients, and -(으)로 for movement directions or tools.

steps.en: I sent a letter to teacher.
At the post office, I sent a thank-you letter to teacher.

ko: 스승의 날이 되어서 오랜만에 고등학교 선생님께 연락을 드렸어요.
직접 찾아뵙지 못해서 정성껏 쓴 편지를 우편으로 보냈어요.
선생님한테서 따뜻한 답장 메시지가 와서 마음이 훈훈해졌어요.
en: It became Teachers' Day, so I contacted my high school teacher after a long time.
Since I couldn't visit in person, I sent a carefully written letter by mail.
A warm reply message arrived from my teacher, so my heart felt warm.

bg-31-04.q: How did the writer send the letter to the teacher?

bg-31-04.why: The text mentions '선생님한테서 따뜻한 답장 메시지가 와서'.

items: I can accurately choose between -한테/-에게 (people), -께 (honorific), and -(으)로 (direction/tools).
I can explain directions and methods of transportation in natural Korean.
